transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

This is a very common issue with Indesit (and other hotpoint/Bosch) tumble dryers. The fact that the noise stops after a few minutes and the drying performance remains unaffected strongly suggests wear on a bearing or bushing rather than a complete mechanical failure.

Here’s a breakdown of what’s likely happening, how to diagnose it, and what you can do about it.

### Most Likely Causes (in order of probability)

1.  Worn Drum Support Bearings/Bushings (Top or Rear)
• Why it squeals: The drum is supported by plastic bushings or ball bearings at the front (top) and rear. Over time, these wear out, lose lubrication, or develop play. When cold, they are tight/stiff. As the dryer runs for a few minutes, friction generates heat, which slightly expands the metal/plastic parts and melts away any residual grease/dust, allowing them to spin more smoothly.
• Symptom: High-pitched squeal or screech at startup that fades as the drum warms up.

2.  Worn Idler Pulley or Tensioner Spring
• Why it squeals: The belt is kept taut by an idler pulley (a small wheel) and a spring. If the pulley’s bearing is dry or worn, it will squeal when cold. As it heats up, the noise may diminish.
• Symptom: Squealing often accompanied by a slight "thumping" if the belt is slipping slightly at first.

3.  Dry or Worn Front Drum Seal (Felt Ring)
• Why it squeals: The front of the drum has a felt seal that rubs against the metal tub. If this dries out, cracks, or loses its lubrication, it can squeal until friction heats and softens the material.
• Symptom: Often accompanied by lint leaking into the motor area over time.

4.  Motor Bearings (Less Likely if Noise Stops)
• If the motor bearings were worn, the noise would typically get worse as it runs, not better. So this is less likely given your description.

---

### How to Diagnose Safely

⚠️ Safety First: Unplug the dryer before inspecting or touching any internal parts.

1.  Check for Loose Objects:
• Open the door and spin the drum by hand. Listen/feel for grinding or catching.
• Check inside the drum for coins, keys, or bra wires that might be trapped between the drum and the tub.

2.  Inspect the Belt and Idler Pulley (Requires removing the top/front panel):
• Remove the top lid (usually two screws at the back) and tilt it forward.
• Locate the belt around the drum, motor pulley, and idler pulley.
• Spin the idler pulley by hand. It should spin smoothly and quietly. If it’s gritty, stiff, or squeaks, replace the idler pulley (cheap part).
• Check if the belt is cracked or glazed.

3.  Check the Front Drum Seal:
• Look at the felt ring around the front of the drum. Is it torn, missing chunks, or dry? If so, replace the front seal.

4.  Check Rear Bearings (More Involved):
• This usually requires removing the entire front panel and drum. If you’re comfortable with DIY, check if the drum wobbles excessively when lifted from the top. Excessive play indicates worn rear bearings or support arms.

---

### Recommended Solutions

#### Option 1: Quick & Cheap Fix (Temporary)
• Lubricate: You can try spraying a dry PTFE lubricant (like WD-40 Specialist Dry Lube) on the idler pulley bearing and the front felt seal. Avoid standard oil/grease as it attracts lint.
• Result: May silence the noise for weeks or months, but doesn’t fix worn parts.

#### Option 2: Replace the Idler Pulley (Most Common Fix)
• Cost: £10–£20 for the part.
• Difficulty: Moderate. Requires removing the top/front panel to access the belt and pulley.
• Why: The idler pulley bearing is a common failure point that causes startup squealing.

#### Option 3: Replace Front Drum Seal & Bushings
• Cost: £15–£30 for parts.
• Difficulty: Moderate to Hard. Requires removing the drum to access the front seal and bushings.
• Why: If the idler pulley is fine, this is the next most likely culprit.

#### Option 4: Replace Rear Bearings (If Drum Wobbles)
• Cost: £20–£40 for parts.
• Difficulty: Hard. Requires full disassembly of the drum assembly.
• Why: Only if you confirm excessive drum play.

---

### When to Call a Professional
• If you’re not comfortable opening the dryer.
• If replacing the idler pulley and seal doesn’t fix it (may indicate motor or complex bearing issues).
• If the noise returns quickly after repair.

### Summary Recommendation
1.  Unplug the dryer.
2.  Inspect the idler pulley (accessible from the top/front panel). Spin it by hand. If it’s noisy, replace it. This is the easiest and most common fix for startup squealing that fades.
3.  If the idler pulley is fine, inspect the front felt seal. Replace if worn/dry.
4.  As a temporary measure, try lubricating the idler pulley bearing with dry PTFE spray.

Given your dryer still dries well and the noise stops, this is almost certainly a wear issue (idler pulley or front seal) rather than a critical failure. Addressing it soon will prevent further damage to the drum or motor.

Thanks. I can't tilt or lay it down because of my back, and I've no special tools. Is there anything I can check from the outside first? The drum feels a bit rough when I turn it by hand and it slightly rocks on one corner.

Given your constraints (no tilting/laying down, no special tools) and the symptoms you’ve described (roughness + rocking on one corner), here’s what you can check from the outside:

### 1. Check for Leveling & Stability (The "Rocking" Issue)
A rocking drum often indicates the dryer isn’t level or is unstable, which can cause misalignment and premature wear.

• Test: Place a spirit level on top of the dryer (or use a phone app). Check front-to-back and side-to-side.
• Fix: Adjust the feet at the bottom. Most Indesit dryers have threaded feet that you can turn by hand:
  • To raise/lower a corner, grip the foot firmly and twist it clockwise or counter-clockwise.
  • Ensure all four feet are firmly on the ground. If one is wobbly, tighten it until the rocking stops.

### 2. Inspect the Drum Seal (Front Felt Ring)
The "roughness" when turning by hand often comes from a dried-out or damaged front drum seal.

• How to check: Shine a flashlight into the gap between the drum and the door opening. Look at the black felt ring.
  • Is it cracked, torn, or missing chunks?
  • Does it look dry or dusty?
• Quick Fix (if accessible): If you can reach behind the seal with your fingers, try applying a small amount of silicone spray or dry PTFE lubricant to the felt edge. Avoid oil-based lubricants as they attract lint. This may reduce roughness temporarily.

### 3. Check for Obstructions
• Remove the lint filter and inspect the drum interior for any foreign objects (coins, keys, bra wires) that might be catching on the seal or drum ribs.
• Look inside the vent hose connection at the back (if accessible from the front) to ensure it’s not blocked.

### 4. Listen Closely at Startup
With the dryer running:
• Place your hand lightly on the side panels near the bottom corners where it rocks. Feel for excessive vibration.
• If the squeal stops after a few minutes, it confirms a cold-start friction issue (likely bearings or seal).

---

### What This Likely Means
The combination of rocking and roughness suggests:
1. The dryer is unlevel, causing uneven wear on the drum supports.
2. The front drum seal/bearing is worn and needs lubrication or replacement.

### Next Steps (Without Special Tools)
1. Level the dryer – This is critical and may reduce stress on the bearings.
2. Lubricate the front seal if accessible.
3. If the noise persists after leveling, the issue is likely internal worn bearings/pulley. Since you can’t tilt the machine, replacement of these parts will require professional help or a very difficult DIY job (removing the back panel while upright).

Would you like guidance on how to adjust the feet safely?
Yes please, how do I adjust the feet? It's on a wooden floor and rocks slightly on one corner. I checked the door seal and filter and found nothing stuck.

Adjusting the feet is usually straightforward and can often be done by hand or with simple household items if you don’t have a wrench. Here’s how to do it safely without tilting the machine:

### Step 1: Gather Your Tools (Household Items)
• Grip Aid: A rubber glove, a dry cloth, or a piece of sandpaper wrapped around your hand will help you grip the plastic foot securely.
• Optional: If it’s very tight, you can use a pair of pliers (wrap the jaws in a cloth to avoid scratching the foot) or an adjustable spanner/wrench if you have one.

### Step 2: Locate the Feet
Look at the four corners at the bottom of the dryer. You’ll see plastic feet that screw into metal threads on the base of the machine.

### Step 3: Adjusting the Foot (The "Rocking" Corner)
Since it rocks on one corner, you need to stabilize that specific foot.

1.  Stabilize the Dryer: Ensure the other three feet are firmly planted. If possible, have someone stand lightly on the opposite side of the dryer to keep it stable while you work (be careful not to put weight on the control panel).
2.  Identify Direction:
    • To raise a corner: Turn the foot counter-clockwise (lefty-loosey).
    • To lower a corner: Turn the foot clockwise (righty-tighty).
3.  Action for the Rocking Corner:
    • Grip the foot of the rocking corner firmly with your cloth/glove.
    • Try turning it counter-clockwise to raise it slightly. This often helps if the floor is uneven and one foot isn’t making full contact.
    • If it’s already raised, try turning it clockwise to lower it until it feels snug against the wood.

### Step 4: Check Levelness
• Use a spirit level or your phone’s level app on top of the dryer.
• The dryer should be perfectly level (or slightly tilted back by about 1–2 degrees, which is often achieved by raising the front feet very slightly). This helps the drum sit correctly and prevents clothes from bunching up.

### Step 5: Lock Nuts (If Present)
Some Indesit models have a small lock nut just above the foot on the metal thread. If you see one:
1.  Loosen it slightly with pliers.
2.  Adjust the foot as described above.
3.  Tighten the lock nut back against the base of the dryer to prevent it from vibrating loose during operation.

### Why This Helps Your Squeal
If the dryer is rocking, the drum shaft can be slightly misaligned or under uneven stress when the motor starts. This puts extra strain on the front bearings and seals. By leveling the machine:
• The drum sits more evenly in its housing.
• The belt tension becomes more consistent.
• Vibration is reduced, which may lessen the initial squeal as the components engage smoothly.

### Next Steps if It Still Rocks or Squeals
If you’ve leveled it and the rocking stops but the squeal persists:
1.  Lubricate the Seal: As mentioned before, try a small amount of silicone spray on the front felt seal (if accessible).
2.  Check the Idler Pulley: If you can see through the bottom grille or vent area, look for the belt tensioner wheel. If it wobbles by hand, that’s likely the source. This usually requires replacement parts and some disassembly, which might be beyond your current constraints.

Would you like tips on how to safely access the idler pulley without laying the dryer down?
Yes please, how can I get at the idler pulley without tilting it? Also I can't really grip the foot very well, it's a bit stiff.

Since you cannot tilt the machine and are having trouble with the feet, let’s address both issues step-by-step.

### Part 1: How to Adjust Stiff Feet Without Tilting

If the feet are stiff and hard to grip, here are three methods to get more leverage without lifting or tilting the dryer:

Method A: The "Sock & Grip" Technique (Best for Hand Adjustment)
1.  Put on a thick rubber glove (like a dishwashing glove) or wrap your hand tightly in a dry, rough cloth. This provides immense friction.
2.  If that’s not enough, try using pliers or an adjustable spanner. Wrap the jaws of the pliers in electrical tape or a cloth to protect the plastic foot from cracking.
3.  Crucial Step: Before turning, ensure the dryer is stable. Have someone stand lightly on the opposite side of the machine (away from the corner you’re adjusting) to keep it steady. This prevents the whole unit from shifting while you turn the foot.

Method B: The "Shim" Method (If You Can’t Turn It)
If the foot is truly stuck and won’t budge, don’t force it—you might strip the thread or break the plastic. Instead:
1.  Find a small, thin piece of material that can act as a shim (a folded piece of thick cardboard, a matchstick, or a small piece of rubber).
2.  Gently lift the rocking corner just enough to slide the shim under the foot.
3.  This will stop the rocking immediately without needing to adjust the thread. You can trim the shim later for a neater look.

Method C: Check for Lock Nuts
Look closely at the base of each foot. Is there a small metal nut just above the plastic foot? If yes, this is a "lock nut" that prevents the foot from moving. You must loosen this nut slightly with pliers before you can turn the foot itself. Once adjusted, tighten it back against the base.

---

### Part 2: Accessing the Idler Pulley Without Tilting

The Hard Truth: The idler pulley is located at the bottom rear of the dryer, inside the casing. It is physically impossible to access or replace it without tilting the machine on its back (or removing the front/rear panels, which is complex and risky for a non-technical user).

However, since you have back issues, here are your options:

1.  Get Help: Ask a friend, neighbor, or family member to help tilt the dryer for just 2 minutes. You can guide them on how to do it safely (tilt onto a soft blanket, support the weight with your knees/chest if needed, not your back).
2.  Call a Professional: A qualified appliance repair technician can access the pulley without you needing to move the machine. This is often worth it if DIY isn’t feasible due to health reasons.

---

### Part 3: What You Can Do From the Outside (While Waiting for Help)

Since you can’t fix the idler pulley right now, focus on what you can do to potentially reduce the noise and wear:

1.  Lubricate the Front Drum Seal:
    • As mentioned before, if the drum feels rough when turning by hand, the front felt seal is likely dry.
    • Use a silicone spray or PTFE lubricant (available at hardware stores). Spray a small amount on a cloth and gently wipe the inside edge of the black rubber/felt seal around the door opening. This can reduce friction and squealing until you get professional help.
